## db2bc2b4fec6

Generator SHA d2e4cdd44b135ca5d00045e20af13c478e102d255439888bbafe58c9366314ab;
canonical Racket hash cfa88dd9ea7d. Evidence is in
checks/audit/db2bc2b4fec6/{input,probes,racket,summary}.json.

### A1 — Reproduced exact-control defect

Call generate(0,0,difficulty='easy',grid_h=6,grid_w=6,n_frames=2). All values are
individually advertised and no joint incompatibility is declared. The generator
returns one frame, not two; self_check returns[]. Requesting n_frames1 gives the
identical input. Exact input (six cells per row):

```text
000000
000000
000111
000101
000111
000000
```

Actual Racket output:

```text
000000
000000
000111
000181
000111
000000
```

The rule correctly fills the only center, so this is NOT a wrong-label finding.
The constructive sampling contract is wrong: anchors on a6×6grid lie in0..3 in
both coordinates; the generator demands separation of at least4 in one coordinate,
so two such frames cannot be placed. After200failed attempts it silently returns
one. The exact-control domain should reject/declare this incompatible request or
change the placement construction rather than claim count2 was honored.

Record1 includes the original controls, seed/index, actual observed count, validator
result, independent center-fill candidate and actual Racket output/hash. Record0
is the one-frame control comparison. Source remains unchanged; fix belongs to its owner.

### A2 — Reproduced validator/domain gap, not label failure

Record2 changes the top-left background cell of A1 from0 to2. self_check still
returns[], because it checks blue coverage/ring centers but never rejects foreign
colors. That input is outside the documented default0/1palette and is not claimed
to be emitted by the generator. Actual Racket preserves the red cell and fills the
blue center correctly. A validator intended to enforce this stated input manifold
should reject it, or the domain documentation should explicitly allow distractors.
This is a syntactic acceptance/domain mismatch, not evidence of corrupted outputs.

All3retained inputs matched the independent center-fill prediction under actual
Racket, with no reference execution errors. Exact invocation:

```bash
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply db2bc2b4fec6 --input ../checks/audit/db2bc2b4fec6/input.json --out ../checks/audit/db2bc2b4fec6/racket.json
```

No false rival or fabricated accidental solve failure was created to satisfy audit
formatting. For A1/A2 the retained candidate agrees with Racket; the defects concern
exact controls and the stated validator domain, respectively.
